municipal_actions: Keep public water points and shade shelters maintained
Monitor the daily forecast update for trend changes
resident_advice: Stay hydrated and use shade during the hottest hours
routine.summary: Routine summer monitoring — no impact-based escalation.

municipal_actions: Run cooling centres on extended or 24-hour schedules
Suspend non-essential outdoor work 11:00–16:00 across municipal projects
Deploy emergency water and shade points at labour gathering spots
Door-to-door wellness checks in high-vulnerability blocks
Pre-position ambulances; activate hospital heat-illness surge plans
Open joint municipal + disaster-management control room
Trigger power emergency protocols for peak demand
resident_advice: Stay in the coolest room you can, especially 12:00–16:00
Visit a cooling centre if your home is unbearable
Never leave anyone — or a pet — in a parked vehicle
Confusion, fainting or hot dry skin is an emergency: seek medical help now

municipal_actions: Open or extend cooling-centre hours (at least 11:00–17:00)
Shift outdoor work hours: avoid 12:00–15:00 for municipal labour
Issue hydration and shade advisories through ward offices
Activate community health-worker checks on elderly and outdoor workers
Prepare ambulance and health-facility heat surge capacity
Coordinate with electricity operations on peak-demand response
resident_advice: Wear light clothing, drink water before you feel thirsty
Watch for cramps, dizziness or nausea — move to shade and rehydrate
Check on elderly relatives, pregnant people and outdoor workers
warning.summary: Dangerous heat expected — municipal heat actions activate.

municipal_actions: Brief field staff and municipal health workers on the outlook
Pre-position ORS and drinking water in high-vulnerability zones
Share the 3–5 day outlook with the power utility demand desk
resident_advice: Plan outdoor work and play for morning or evening
Keep water with you and check on elderly neighbours
watch.summary: Heat is building — prepare, do not activate yet.

alert_levels.summary: Routine summer monitoring — no impact-based escalation.
Heat is building — prepare, do not activate yet.

data_source: synthetic demo scenario 'heat-plus-pollution' — deterministic, offline, generated by core/demo.py
demo_disclaimer: Demo / synthetic scenario — not a live forecast or observation.
granularity_note: Zones are ~10 km model grid points, not ward-level observations. Do not read a single zone value as a street-level measurement.
persistence_rule: IMD plains departure rule (Tmax ≥ 40 °C AND departure ≥ 4.5 °C from the fixed 1991–2020 normal) marks a daily candidate; only runs of ≥ 2 consecutive candidate days are declared heatwave episodes. Single candidates stay labelled as early watches.

scenario.data_source: synthetic demo scenario 'heat-plus-pollution' — deterministic, offline, generated by core/demo.py
scenario.demo_disclaimer: Demo / synthetic scenario — not a live forecast or observation.
scenario.issued_at_note: Fixed scenario timestamp (intentional): the demo clock never moves, so 'Day +3' is always 2026-05-21 regardless of when you open the demo.
scenario.label: Severe heat + hazardous air pollution
scenario.summary: A stagnant, near-windless spell traps dust and combustion PM2.5 under strong heat. Tmax approaches 48 °C in the densest zones (a severe heatwave episode on Days +2 to +5) WHILE PM2.5 peaks push the indicative Indian AQI into the 400s. The joint heat+air load band reaches Severe, lifting recommended actions a level.
scenario.tagline: Compound exposure: the joint heat+air load escalates.
teaching_points: Concentration AQI stays separate from the parameterised joint load
Stagnant wind raises both WBGT (less convective cooling) and PM2.5
Escalation rule: severe air load + thermal ≥ warning ⇒ severe alert level

thermal_method.assumption_no_anomaly: climate-normal departure unavailable — HTSI score computed from meteorological stress only, without the acclimatisation anomaly term

estimated.meaning: Computed from model/forecast inputs (temperature, humidity, wind, shortwave radiation) with the documented formula. All required inputs were present. This is NOT a globe-thermometer measurement.

measured.meaning: Observed by a physical instrument at the location.

partial-input.meaning: Computed with at least one required input missing and replaced by the documented assumption listed in `assumptions`. Treat as lower-confidence than `estimated`.

unavailable.meaning: A mandatory input (air temperature or relative humidity) is missing. No value is produced — we never invent one.

thermal_method.score_formula: HTSI = 100 · clip((WBGT_est − 25) / (36 − 25), 0, 1)^1.4 + min(8, 1.6 · max(0, Tmax − Tmax_normal(1991–2020))) when a fixed climate normal is available; clipped to 0–100. The anomaly term represents acclimatisation stress: heat further above the local normal harms more at the same absolute WBGT.

vulnerability.formula: vulnerability = 100 · (0.30·norm(pop_density) + 0.22·norm(elderly_pct) + 0.20·norm(outdoor_worker_pct) + 0.16·(1 − cooling_access/100) + 0.12·norm(illiteracy_pct)); norm() is min–max across the demo zone set. Inputs are a SYNTHETIC labelled profile (see zone_profiles source).
